about: Wrong answers that point to a specific misunderstanding about ratios and percents. 'pointsTo' is the subskill to work on. Claude's draft (2026-11-20).

misconceptions.description: Adds the same amount instead of multiplying (3 : 4 = 12 : 13, because 3 + 9 = 12).
Mixes up which number goes with which in the ratio.
Divides the wrong way for a unit rate (4 ÷ $12 instead of $12 ÷ 4).
Multiplies instead of dividing to find the amount for one.
Picks the lower total price instead of the lower price for each one.
Multiplies the wrong pair of numbers when cross-multiplying.
Moves the decimal point the wrong number of places (7% = 0.7; 0.4 = 4%).
Writes the same number with or without the % sign (35% = 35; 0.4 = 0.4%).
Writes the fraction's numbers as the percent (3/5 = 35%).
Divides the number by the percent (25% of 80 = 80 ÷ 25).
Multiplies by the percent but forgets it's out of 100 (25% of 80 = 2000).
Divides the whole by the part (12 is 400% of 48).
Gives the part as the percent (12 out of 48 = 12%).
Gives only the amount of the change (the discount or the tip), not the new amount.
Adds a discount or subtracts an increase.
Subtracts (or adds) the percent number itself ($40 − 25 = $15).
Divides the change by the new amount instead of the original.
Gives the amount of the change as the percent (50 -> 40 is a 10% decrease).
